content:
morgan: Quick sync — ran FP8 enablement smoke on H100 + L40S. Seeing intermittent warmup jitter and a handful of KV-cache evictions when kernel selection flips. Put profiler extracts below and a small proposal.

liam: yup saw this on L40S too. Pattern: seq_len jumps (128->512) trigger kernel handoff at batch boundary, throughput drops ~15-20% temporarily.

anya: attaching condensed flame snippet from perf
```
# top stacks (sampled)
transformer_forward::fp8_kernel_A 40%
transformer_forward::fallback_int8 18%
kv_cache::lookup 12%
batch_manager::handoff 9%
others 21%
```

kai: interesting that `batch_manager::handoff` shows up so high. suspect our handoff check is running per-batch and doing expensive kernel rebinds. we should debounce handoffs for X batches.

morgan: current transformer engine env: `TRANSFORMER_ENGINE_FP8=1 KERNEL_SELECTION_MODE=auto HANDOFF_DEBOUNCE=1` — that's probably too eager. proposal: HANDOFF_DEBOUNCE -> 3, and only allow kernel switch if (avg_seq_len over last N requests) > threshold AND no KV-eviction in last M ms.

liam: ran benchmarks with a local patch (debounce=3). numbers (1000 requests mix):
```
H100 FP8 kernel_A: median 6.8ms/token, p95 12.3ms
H100 fallback INT8: median 9.5ms/token, p95 18.4ms
L40S FP8 kernel_A: median 8.9ms/token, p95 16.7ms
L40S fallback INT8: median 12.1ms/token, p95 23.2ms
kernel-switch events per-req: down from 0.27 -> 0.03
```
reduction in kernel-switch correlates with fewer KV evictions.

anya: one caveat — FP8 calibration edge-case: when calibration map is stale across shards we occasionally see degraded logits (small) and very rare NaN on extreme inputs. not observed in unit tests but showed up in a long tail of fuzz runs.

kai: to address that we should: 1) materialize per-shard calibration table with versioning, 2) make kernel handoff refuse FP8 if calibration mismatch, 3) expose a `--force-fp8` for bench runs.

morgan: ok. patch sketch (will PR):
```diff
- if seq_len_change: switch_kernel()
+ if seq_len_change and debounce_passed and !kv_eviction_recent and calib_ok: switch_kernel()
```
also add metric `kernel_switch_count` and `kv_eviction_count` to per-request trace.

infra-bot: deploy-start: rollout/eng-runtime/fp8-debounce-v0.1 -> canary 10% @1912345800

devex: can we add an opt-in query param for customers who want aggressive fp8? something like `?inference.prefs.fp8=aggressive` so we don't surprise prod.

liam: ran a focused stress with high-concurrency (400 qps) and the new debounce lowered p95 by ~9% on H100 and cut evictions by 70%. still seeing rare(0.1%) requests that spike — digging.

anya: adding checklist for follow-ups:
- per-shard calibration versioning (owner: anya)
- handoff debounce default -> 3 (owner: kai)
- trace fields for kernel_switch_count / kv_eviction (owner: morgan)
- add e2e smoke that ramps seq_len mid-request (owner: liam)

sre-bot: alert: p95 spike observed during canary at 1912345910 (auto-throttle engaged). No user-facing errors.

morgan: noted. we’ll pause canary if new spikes reproduce. thanks all — will open PRs and test harness changes, assigning items above. :thumbsup:

kai: also proposal: instead of hard debounce, consider a weighted EWMA on seq_len and only switch when weight > W to smooth transient bursts. more work but less brittle.

liam: agree EWMA looks cleaner for production. will prototype after current patches.

morgan: summary action: quick-win debounce=3 + calib gating + traces. longer-term: EWMA + adaptive batching heuristic to avoid switching mid-batch.

sre-bot: noted. closing incident if no further regressions in next 24h. :eyes:
